note: 지면(.astro)에 손으로 적은 정정을 기계가 읽을 수 있게 옮겨 둔 것. 기사 정정은 앞말(frontmatter)에서 자동으로 온다. 새 정정을 지면에 적으면 여기에도 적어야 하고, 안 적으면 scripts/check-corrections.mjs 가 잡는다.

rows.what: Korean catalogue size and total hours
rows.why: Korean titles were matched by title text against a Wikidata list. 52 titles Netflix classes on its English-language charts — The Perfect Couple, Suits, The Circle, Hit Man among them — were counted as Korean. Netflix splits its charts by a title's primary language, so only the Non-English charts are counted now. Hand-checking the largest remaining titles removed 8 more.
Same cause as /watched. The page was published after the correction and has never shown the wrong totals, but it rests on the corrected set and says so.

rows.what: Exports by type of company, and the unattributed residual
rows.why: KOSIS table DT_113_STBL_1025706 classifies on two levels — form of export above, type of company below — and returns only the lower name, so several rows a year read 'terrestrial broadcasters' and differ by code alone. We had taken the finished-programme row for three of the four company types while the fourth entered whole. Each type is now the sum of every export form published for it. The residual we described as unattributed did not exist; we had not added it up.

Companies that disclose headcount but not pay were left in the denominator, so their staff were averaged in as if they earned nothing — 456 people in content and 20,613 across the market. Pay is now weighted over disclosing companies only. Tenure, headcount and the gender split come from companies that disclose them and did not move.

rows.from: included Teach You a Lesson (China) and The East Palace (China) as Korean
rows.to: both removed; titles whose name is shared with a foreign work are now flagged in place
rows.why: The front page data file was hand-made and could not be rebuilt, so it did not follow when the matching rule was corrected. It is now built by a script from the same rule as every other page.

rows.what: Korean titles charting in six Southeast Asian markets
rows.why: Same matching cause. 42 titles were not Korean — among them two Witcher animations, I Am Legend and Elysium. The distribution the page describes did not change shape; it sharpened.

rows.what: The table of longest-running and fiercest Korean titles
rows.from: listed Teach You a Lesson (China) as the second fiercest, plus The Perfect Couple and Run Away (United States) and The Empress (Germany)
rows.why: Same cause as the front page — a hand-made data file that could not follow a corrected rule. It is now built by a script.

rows.what: The note listing what the region table leaves out
rows.from: said the survey’s “Unclassified” region carries no value in any year
rows.to: names the year it does carry one — 2005, where it is 89.1% of the total
rows.why: The sentence was written by hand and never measured. 2005 is the year with the least regional detail, and the largest cell in it was the one we called empty. The page now reads the exception out of the data.

rows.what: The size of the Southeast Asia panel and everything counted from it
rows.from: 405 titles, 204 of them unverifiable by language label
rows.why: Eight titles were in a Korean panel although our own attribution query — the one that produces the shared/unambiguous split we publish — returned no Korean work for those exact names: Waterworld, Re/Member, Into the Storm, Wildflower, Feng Shui, Glorious Days, Long Live Love! and You and Me. This was not a judgement call; it was our list contradicting our own instrument. A check now fails the build if any panel title is in that state.

rows.what: What reaching number one is worth
rows.from: Reaching number one doubles the hours. It adds no weeks. (2.5x on means of the top 50 by hours)
rows.to: 4.3x on medians of all 235 titles, and five median weeks against two — then 1.20x once run length is held fixed among titles that lasted six to ten weeks
rows.why: The peak-group table was computed on the fifty largest titles by hours. Inside that group every title has already had a long run, so run length looked irrelevant when it is in fact what put those titles in the group. Recomputed on all 235 titles, with medians beside means because one title holds 5.05bn of 23.72bn hours.

rows.what: How many K-pop acts fall outside the attention panel
rows.from: Acts with no English Wikipedia article are invisible — and we cannot say how many there are
rows.to: 1,312 of 2,128 Korean musical groups (61.7%) and 3,987 of 5,408 singers (73.7%) are outside the panel; 3,572 of those singers have a Korean Wikipedia article
rows.why: The panel is built on English Wikipedia pageviews, so we treated the missing acts as uncountable. Wikidata records the same acts whether or not English Wikipedia does, and we already query it for the roster. Counting with and without an English sitelink gives a floor on the blind spot.

rows.what: Which Netflix titles count as Korean — the rule itself, and the figures in eight articles measured through it
rows.from: A title counted as Korean if its text matched any Wikidata label of a Korean work, in any language. 23 titles written in Arabic, Hebrew, Cyrillic and Japanese script matched that way (37,962 Korean chart places).
rows.to: Non-Latin labels are ignored, because Netflix does not translate titles in these lists. 37,750 Korean chart places; both figures round to 7.7% of the world chart, so the headline did not move. Figures moved in eight articles — the-share-that-did-not-grow, six-titles-or-forty-nine, korean-titles-climb, home-chart-is-not-a-gate, land-or-spread, it-moved-it-did-not-shrink, reaching-number-one-is-mostly-length and music-has-no-squid-game-and-is-more-concentrated-anyway — and all eight were rewritten from the data rather than by hand where a table was involved.
rows.why: Our rule for deciding which Netflix titles are Korean matched title text against Wikidata labels in any language, so 23 titles written in Arabic, Hebrew, Cyrillic and Japanese script were counted as Korean. They are local works: Netflix does not translate titles in these lists — Squid Game holds 445 places across ten Arab markets under its Latin name, and only 10 of the 1,530 distinct titles on Egypt's chart are written in Arabic script. The rule now ignores non-Latin labels. Across the whole site this moved Korea's share of world chart places from 37,962 places to 37,750, both of which round to 7.7%.

rows.what: Nineteen of the 2,238 places we called Korean are not in Korea, and one of them led a column
rows.from: The most-read Korean place on the Vietnamese Wikipedia was given as the Battle of Khe Sanh, at 62.52 reads per million. The panel held 2,238 places.
rows.to: The Battle of Khe Sanh is fought in Vietnam and is no longer in the panel. The Vietnamese column now opens with President of South Korea at 46.88. The panel holds 2,219 places, and the nineteen we removed are listed on the page with their coordinates.
rows.why: The places were selected on Wikidata's country property (P17). That property records involvement as well as location: the Battle of Khe Sanh carries South Korea because South Korea fought there, and the Order of Friars Minor, two Korean Air crash sites, and the Antarctic Jang Bogo Station entered the same way. We re-tested every place against its coordinates instead, because a location does not follow a belligerent. The nineteen accounted for 4.61% of all reads in the panel. Our first attempt at this check also used the country property and reported no problem at all — a check that reuses the ruler being checked always agrees with it.

causes.title-text: Korean titles were matched by English title text alone, so foreign works with the same name were counted as Korean
causes.kosis-two-level: A KOSIS table classifies on two levels and returns only one of them unless both are asked for
causes.pay-denominator: Companies that disclose headcount but not pay were left in the denominator
causes.unmeasured-sentence: A sentence about the data was written by hand and never measured against it
causes.miscounted-corrections: Our own corrections article counted the corrections wrong — it swept in a correction from another day and asserted a single cause the record does not support
causes.attribution-contradiction: Our own attribution query returned no Korean work for a title that was nonetheless in our Korean panel — the list and the instrument we publish disagreed
causes.selected-on-outcome: A comparison was computed on the fifty largest titles by hours — a group selected on the very outcome being explained — and reported as if it described the whole panel
causes.limit-never-tested: A limitation was written down as unmeasurable and never tested — the number turned out to be reachable from a source we already query
causes.ruler-fixed-upstream: A rule that decides which titles count was corrected, and every number measured through it moved. The article was right about what it was given; what it was given was wrong.
causes.selector-not-location: A panel of places was selected on Wikidata's country property, which records who was involved as well as where a thing is. Places entered the list because Korea took part in something that happened elsewhere.
causes.roster-widened: The set of titles a figure was measured over was widened after publication, and every count measured through it moved. Nothing in the earlier figures was wrong for the set they described; the set was too small for a median to hold still.
causes.definition-inconsistent: A word we publish on many pages — median — was computed one way here and another way everywhere else. A reader comparing two of our pages had no way to know the same word meant two different things.
causes.window-too-short: A measurement window was short enough that its own highest month became the peak. Widening the window moved the peaks and exposed a limit the first version could not see at all.
causes.no-row-to-be-counted-in: A value existed but had no row in the table that counts it, so our own check could report it as neither present nor missing. Not a miscount — an absence of the place where the count happens.
causes.spelling-case: Netflix chart text and Wikidata labels write the same work with different letter case, and matching them exactly dropped Korean titles out of the set as though they did not exist

guardNote: A guard is a check that fails the build if this kind of mistake recurs. Null means we have not written one yet — it is a work list, not a claim of coverage.
